comments.note: APIMethodParameter validates method existence against the live method index. Test stubs that use processReturn() must therefore live in the TestDriver's API folder (tests/application/assets/classes/TestDriver/API/) to be included in the discovered index — stubs placed only in AppFrameworkTestClasses/ are invisible to the validator. This is worth documenting in testing.md as a gotcha.

The test environment has no committed config files for the local DB/UI/CAS — only .dist templates exist (tests/application/config/). The test suite cannot run without setting up real credentials, and the dist files contain root/empty-password defaults that do not work on most local environments. Consider either shipping a working fallback or documenting the exact setup steps in testing.md.

CacheableAPIMethodTrait::getCacheFile() builds the JSON file path directly from APICacheManager::getMethodCacheFolder() but does not ensure the method-specific subfolder exists before writing. The JSONFile::putData() call will fail if the directory is missing. APICacheManager::getMethodCacheFolder() should either create the folder, or writeToCache() should call FileHelper::createFolder() before writing.

comments.note: CacheableAPIMethodTrait::getCacheKey() uses serialize() to hash parameters: md5(...serialize($params)). For the intended use (associative string→scalar arrays), this works correctly, but json_encode() with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR would be strictly more portable: it cannot accidentally trigger __sleep() on objects, produces shorter strings for the same data, and is more explicit about the constraint that parameter values must be JSON-serialisable scalars. Consider changing to json_encode(ksort($params) or json_encode($params, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR) in a follow-up.

CacheableAPIMethodTrait::readFromCache() calls $cacheFile->parse() without a try-catch. If the cache file is corrupted (e.g., a partially-written JSON from a previous crash), the parse exception propagates uncaught through _process(), failing the request entirely instead of falling back to fresh computation. A defensive try-catch around parse() that returns null on any exception would make the cache layer resilient to file corruption.

APICacheStrategyTest::setUp() assigns $this->tempFolder = sys_get_temp_dir().'/api-cache-manager-'.uniqid() but the variable is never read anywhere in the class — neither in tearDown() nor in any test method. All manager tests use APICacheManager::getMethodCacheFolder() directly. The $tempFolder property and its assignment are dead code and should be removed.

FixedDurationStrategy and ManualOnlyStrategy both lack class-level PHPDoc blocks. All other new cache classes (APICacheManager, CacheableAPIMethodTrait, CacheableAPIMethodInterface, APIResponseCacheLocation) have proper @package/@subpackage annotations and descriptive class-level comments. The two strategy classes should be brought to the same standard for consistency.

APICacheStrategyInterface::getID() is declared and implemented in both strategies but is not exercised by any test in APICacheStrategyTest. The method is unused by the cache-aside machinery in BaseAPIMethod._process() as well — it is currently dead API surface. Either add tests for it, or document its intended future use (e.g., for cache statistics or strategy-aware invalidation) to justify keeping it in the interface.
